pride_data.title: Structural insights into protein-RNA interactions within biomolecular condensates using UV cross-linking and mass spectrometry
pride_data.projectDescription: UV-light-induced protein-RNA cross-linking followed by MS analysis was used to identify the interaction sites between protein and RNA in different phase-separated and non-phase separated states of complexes involving the following proteins: PTBP1, FUS, and SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Protein-RNA complexes were reconstituted under different conditions and cross-linked by 254-nm UV light in a Spectrolinker device (2.4 J cm-2). For phase-separated systems, condensed and dispersed phases were separated before or after the cross-linking step, and before the following processing steps. Samples were ethanol precipitated and digested with RNases (T1 and A, additionally benzonase for PTBP1 and FUS) and trypsin. For the nucleocapsid protein complex, differential 16O/18O labeling using ATP was performed as described in Goetze et al., Anal. Chem., 2021. Peptide-RNA adducts were enriched from the digested samples by titanium dioxide metal affinity chromatography and analyzed by data-dependent LC-MS/MS on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos instrument. Data was acquired with stepped HCD collision energies (23 ± 5%). Precursor and fragment ions were detected in the orbitrap analyzer. Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.5, and the RNxQuest add-on (Sarnowski et al., J. Proteome Res., 2023). Sequence databases contained the forward and reversed sequences of the target proteins and the sequences of the RNAs, respectively. RNA adducts of up to four nucleotides and different neutral loss types were considered according to Sarnowski et al., bioRxiv, 2022. Additional search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 10 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 20 ppm. A 1% false discovery rate cut-off at the unique peptide-RNA conjugate level was defined for RNxQuest to control the error rate for identifications.  A file list document connects the individual result tables to the raw files and sample types. Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
